method_inputs.rationale: Bear case for SoFi as a bank holding company. Revenue grows 38 percent in FY2026 on the FY2025 net revenue base of 3613.4m (revenue 4986.5m), then 10, 6, 4 and 3 percent. Pre-tax margin is 12 percent in 2026, 9 percent in 2027 and 8 percent thereafter. Loan growth is 36, 10, 7, 5 and 4 percent. Net income is pre-tax profit times (1 minus the 8.71 percent normalised tax rate). Retained equity is the change in risk-weighted assets times a 16.9 percent CET1 target. Discount rate is the 13.09 percent CAPM cost of equity, which is unverified because beta is unverified. Terminal value is 7x 2030 net income, a total-earnings multiple. Value is negative because capital retention and stock-based pay exceed earnings in every year, so the bear case is a permanent-loss case on this method.
source_notes: Operating scenario: bear. Revenue growth 0.38 in FY2026 against FY2025 net revenue of 3613.4m gives 4986.5m; then 0.10, 0.06, 0.04 and 0.03 (analyst assumptions). Revenue and FY2025 base from the stored net revenue history and the operating scenario set.

Pre-tax margin driver (pre-tax proxy on total net revenue): 0.12 in 2026, 0.09 in 2027, 0.08 in 2028 to 2030. Pre-tax profit is 598.4, 493.7, 465.1, 483.8 and 498.3m. Unverified because consolidated operating income for Q3 2026 is not captured.

Net income = pre-tax profit x (1 - 0.0871), using the stored normalised tax rate of 8.71 percent (median quarterly effective rate, financial analytics artifact 68d0d7b1). Net income is 546.2, 450.6, 424.6, 441.6 and 454.9m.

Depreciation and amortisation at 7.0 percent of revenue (349.1, 384.0, 407.0, 423.3, 436.0m). Capex at 7.5 percent of revenue (374.0, 411.4, 436.1, 453.5, 467.1m), an analyst assumption; the Q3 2026 capex actual is not captured. Net D&A less capex is about -25 to -31m a year.

Retained equity (change_in_net_working_capital, a positive use of cash): change in risk-weighted assets x 16.9 percent holding-company CET1 ratio at 30 Sep 2026 (10-Q, source 2e9b4dba; RWA 56,204.0m at 30 Sep 2026). RWA at 31 Dec 2025 is about 37,160m, derived from CET1 capital 8,473.5m at 22.8 percent (source 030641d0). FY2026 uses 9/30 RWA as the year-end proxy, giving 3218.4m retained in 2026. From 2027, RWA grows with the bear loan growth of 10, 7, 5 and 4 percent: retention is 949.8, 731.9, 559.0 and 469.6m. Loan growth is a proxy for RWA growth (analyst assumption). sections.title: Judgment: returns on bank capital are not yet proven

paragraphs.text: SoFi's central question is whether its member growth and bank-funded lending can earn a return on equity above its cost of equity after credit losses, regulatory capital and the Galileo and Technisys investment. On the evidence reviewed, that is not yet proven. Reported profit has grown quickly: GAAP net income was 240,989 thousand in Q3 2026 against 139,392 thousand a year earlier, and 564,312 thousand over the nine months to 30 September 2026 against 307,771 thousand. Trailing twelve-month net income is 737.9 million. Cash, capital and share-count measures do not yet follow that profit.

Capital has absorbed much of the growth. Holding-company CET1 capital rose from 8,473,542 thousand at 31 December 2025 to 9,520,479 thousand at 30 September 2026, but the CET1 ratio fell from 22.8% to 16.9% because total loans rose from 38.0 billion to 53.7 billion over the same nine months. SoFi Bank's CET1 ratio fell from 16.4% to 14.9%, against a 7.0% minimum and a 6.5% well-capitalised level. The holding company states that, under Federal Reserve policy, it generally would not have funds free of restrictions for dividends on regulatory capital instruments at 30 September 2026.

Growth is also being paid for in shares. Diluted weighted average shares rose from 1,185.5 million in Q1 2025 to 1,357.8 million in Q3 2026, and period-end common shares rose 7.6% year on year to 1,296.6 million. Per-share earnings therefore grew more slowly than net income. Trailing stock-based compensation was 288.3 million, about 39% of trailing net income, and the quarterly ratio of stock-based compensation to revenue sits near the bottom of its own history (5.1% latest against a 9.7% median). Dilution is a real cost to holders even though no cash leaves the company. The 2025 common stock issuance of about 3.2 billion that supported the 2025 ratios is reported in the regulatory capital discussion but has not been traced to a checked passage, so it stays unverified.

On a crude basis, the return is below the cost of equity. Trailing net income of 737.9 million against invested capital of 8,485.6 million at 30 September 2026 gives about 8.7% (derived). The invested-capital measure is a non-bank definition, equity plus long-term debt less cash and securities, and the cost of equity of 13.09% rests on an unverified beta of 1.88 and a 4.23% equity risk premium. The gap is therefore indicative rather than proven, and quarterly ROE on bank equity cannot yet be computed for all twenty quarters. What the filings do show is a rising denominator: invested capital rose about 53% in nine months (derived), and returns on that new capital are not yet visible in cash.

Cash conversion is the weakest part of the record. Trailing free cash flow was negative 8,793 million at Q2 2026, against a twenty-quarter median of negative 3,985 million, and the latest value sits at about the 16th percentile of the window. Free cash flow to net income was negative 13.8 times at Q2 2026 against a median of negative 5.8 times. Operating cash outflow of 6,205 million in the first half of 2026 (against 1,445 million a year earlier) is attributed mainly to loans held for sale, where originations outpaced paydowns and sales. Capex ran at 1.11 times depreciation and amortisation at Q2 2026 against a median of 0.64 times.

Credit is improving in aggregate but the card book is the risk to watch. The total net charge-off ratio fell to 1.62% in Q3 2026 from 2.04% in Q1 2026, 2.07% in FY2025 and 2.63% in FY2024. Card net charge-offs fell to 6.68% annualised in Q1 2026 from 10.89% a year earlier, yet card loans rose to about 40% of loans at 30 June 2026 from 28%, and the allowance ratio rose to 4.29% from 3.30%. Management's own hypothetical 10% rise in credit loss rates would reduce pre-tax income by 257.7 million over twelve months, which is about 54% of FY2025 reported net income of 481.3 million. Whether the 1.62% figure is a base rate depends on loss rates through a full cycle, and management's target band by product is not disclosed, so the credit falsifier cannot yet be applied.

The funding advantage is supported internally but untested externally. Net interest margin was 5.98% in Q2 2026 and net interest income 788.2 million, up 52% year on year. Management says the average deposit rate in Q2 2026 was 156 basis points below the rate on warehouse facilities, worth about 712.6 million annualised. That comparison is a wholesale funding comparison, not a market deposit benchmark, and no FDIC survey or Ally and Nu deposit-rate series was obtained. The 50 basis point deposit-cost falsifier therefore cannot be tested. As a sensitivity only, a 50 basis point repricing of the 51.3 billion deposit base would cost about 256.5 million a year before tax (derived), roughly one third of the 737.9 million trailing net income.

The Galileo and Technisys platform cannot yet be shown to earn on its own. Its filed net revenue was 450.2 million in FY2025 with contribution profit of 144.4 million (32%). Contribution then fell from 47.9 million in Q4 2025 to 12.0 million in Q1 2026 and 11.8 million in Q2 2026, after a large client left and technology services fees fell. Intercompany revenue from SoFi's own businesses rose, and the analytics series reports platform revenue of 360.8 million for FY2025, which does not reconcile to the filed 450.2 million. Segment operating income after corporate allocations is not captured, so the platform is carried as a range from zero to the 144.4 million pre-allocation contribution, not as an earner.

Valuation on the capital-constrained equity method does not support the 14.28 price in any case. Value per diluted share is -1.79 in the bear case, 1.13 in the base case and 6.74 in the bull case, giving a probability-weighted value of 1.38 at 30%, 50% and 20% weights. The base case discounts an explicit-year present value of -5,331.0 million and a terminal present value of 6,867.1 million, giving equity value of 1,536.1 million over 1,357.8 million diluted shares. The 13.09% cost of equity is built from a 5.12% ten-year Treasury yield, which is verified, and an unverified beta. Measured to 2030 at today's multiple, the no-rerating return is +55.3% in the base case (9.2% annualised), -65.3% in the bear case and +203.3% in the bull case. Measured as the undiscounted return from each terminal price target to the market price, the base case is -34.5%. These are two different measures and should not be read as one return. Because explicit equity cash flows are negative in every case, the terminal value share of enterprise value (4.47 in the base case) is not a share of positive value and is reported only as an indicator of dependence on the terminal assumption.

The permanent-loss case lies below the bear case. In the bear case, explicit equity cash flows sum to -5,215.8 million undiscounted and equity value is -2,435.6 million. The tail that would cause permanent loss is credit losses moving above the bear stress (net charge-offs of 2.6% in 2026 and 3.0% thereafter) while the bank still retains capital to grow loans. In that case the 2026 capital shortfall of about 2,952 million would have to be met by new equity, roughly 207 million shares at 14.28 (illustrative and derived), with the holder's claim diluted before any terminal value. A 10% rise in credit loss rates alone would remove 257.7 million of pre-tax income over twelve months.

Management's alignment is documented in part. The Compensation Committee members are independent under Nasdaq standards and the consultant reports to the committee chair. Those facts argue against weak governance, but they do not show that pay follows per-share outcomes, because incentive metrics, the award table and related-party tables are not in the extracts reviewed. No cash has been returned to shareholders in the window, and the trend in share count and stock compensation means that the holder's claim depends on capital retention and dilution rather than payout. Management has been candid about funding savings but has not benchmarked them against a market deposit rate, and that benchmark is the test management's funding strategy most needs.

Confidence is low on the valuation and forecast, moderate on reported history and credit, and low on the platform and funding claims. The forecast revenue path is not reconciled to September loan balances: full-year 2026 growth rates imply a fourth-quarter revenue fall in the bear case and a near-flat or modest rise in the base and bull cases, and the 2026 flows partly double-count nine months already in the 30 September balance sheet. The decision is therefore withheld. The view would change if a verified capital roll-forward showed loan growth funded mainly from retained earnings and holding-company CET1 held near its current level without new equity, if deposit cost stayed within about 50 basis points of a market benchmark for four quarters, or if platform segment profit after allocations turned clearly positive.

sections.implication: The decision is withheld. On the evidence reviewed, SoFi's lending and fee franchise may earn above its cost of equity, but that has not been demonstrated. The equity is not supported at 14.28 on this method, the bear case is a permanent-loss case in capital terms, and the monitoring thresholds should be read as the tests that would change this judgment: holding-company CET1 toward the 10% bear threshold, sustained negative cash conversion after bank capital, card losses above management's band, and platform contribution that does not recover after allocations.

sections.counterevidence: The bearish reading has real limits. Holding-company and bank CET1 ratios remain far above their minimums, SoFi Bank is classed as well capitalised, and liquidity reserves were 15.9 billion with 13.3 billion unused at 30 September 2026. Total net charge-offs fell year on year, net interest margin widened, and trailing net income rose sharply. Operating cash outflows are attributed to held-for-sale timing that could reverse if loan sales catch up, and the negative explicit cash flows largely reflect the capital that loan growth consumes, which would shrink if growth slowed. Against these points, the probability-weighted value sits far below the market price, and the base-case annualised no-rerating return of 9.2% is below the cost of equity.
